en.title: Merge Overlapping Closed Intervals
en.description:
Merge overlapping closed intervals and output the non-overlapping intervals in ascending order of start. Touching at the same endpoint counts as overlapping, but adjacent integer endpoints that are not equal do not. The original example input contains [1,23], so the correct result is [[1,23]]; the original output was mistakenly computed as if it were [1,2].

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n lines of start end; 1≤n≤100000, 1≤start≤end≤1000000000. The original constraint intervals[i][2] is a typo involving the endpoint index; it is restored as bounds on the two endpoints.
en.output: The first line is the number of merged intervals, followed by one line per interval with its two endpoints, in ascending order of start.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 1 / 1 23; 2 / 1 3 / 5 5; 2 / 1 1 / 2 2. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Sort by start and maintain the last merged segment; if the new start does not exceed its end, extend it, otherwise start a new segment.
